# Review pack: review-security-input-injection (java)

## File: `references/languages/java.md`

### Detection signals — Java (Security: Input & Injection)

Detection signals only. They cite no standard. Report findings against the element IDs listed (defined in
`../standards/`). A signal is evidence only when untrusted data reaches it or the setting is explicit (`SKILL.md`
step 3). The only Java defaults a worker may rely on are those stated in `java-input.md` (JVA-12, JVA-14, JVA-15).
Spring Boot multipart limits, Thymeleaf and SnakeYAML version defaults are not localized: report explicit values only,
and add a `localized-standard-gap` note for a missing setting.

| Signal (API, setting or pattern) | Look in | Indicates | Element(s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Statement.execute*` with concatenation; `JdbcTemplate.query(sql + v)`; `String.format` into SQL | DAOs, repositories | SQL built from untrusted values | JVA-03, SQL-01 |
| `createQuery`/`createNativeQuery` with `+`; `@Query("… " + …)` | JPA repositories, services | JPQL/HQL/native injection | JVA-01, SQL-02 |
| `prepareCall("{call p('" + v + "')}")`; `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` with concatenation in PL/SQL | DAOs, `*.sql` | Procedure injection | SQL-03 |
| `JpaSort.unsafe(` with request data; `Sort.by(request…)` into `@Query`; `ORDER BY " + sort` | repositories, controllers | Unallowlisted sort/identifiers | JVA-14, SQL-04 |
| `@Query` `LIKE '%" + …` or `LIKE CONCAT` built from input in native queries | repositories | Hand-built LIKE | JVA-15 |
| `spring.datasource.username=root`/`postgres`/`sa` | `application*.properties/yml` | Over-privileged database account | SQL-07 |
| `Runtime.getRuntime().exec(String)`; `ProcessBuilder` with request data; `"sh", "-c"` / `"cmd", "/c"` with input | services | Command injection | JVA-04, INJ-04, INJ-05 |
| `ScriptEngineManager…eval`, SpEL `parseExpression(input)`, OGNL/EL evaluation of input | services, controllers | Expression/script injection | JVA-06, INJ-03, A05-07 |
| `InitialContext.lookup(input)`; LDAP `search(…, "(uid=" + v + ")")`; `XPath.evaluate("…" + v)` | directory/XML code | JNDI/LDAP/XPath injection | JVA-06, INJ-06 |
| `DocumentBuilderFactory`/`SAXParserFactory`/`XMLInputFactory`/`TransformerFactory`/`SchemaFactory` used on untrusted XML without explicit `FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING`, `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD/SCHEMA/STYLESHEET` or `disallow-doctype-decl` | XML parsing code | External connections not restricted | JVA-12, XML-02 |
| `setXIncludeAware(true)`; `IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES = true`; FSP set `false` | XML parsing code | XML inclusion enabled | JVA-05, XML-01 |
| DTD support left on (`jdk.xml.dtd.support` unset) where no DTD is needed | XML config | DTDs not disabled | JVA-13 |
| `ObjectInputStream.readObject`/`readUnshared` without `setObjectInputFilter` / `jdk.serialFilter` | consumers, caches, servlets | Unfiltered Java deserialization | JVA-10, JVA-02, DES-05 |
| `XMLDecoder`; XStream without allowlist; `new Yaml()` without `SafeConstructor`; `kryo.setRegistrationRequired(false)`; fastjson autotype | serializers | Unsafe deserialization libraries | DES-05, DES-06 |
| Jackson `enableDefaultTyping`/`activateDefaultTyping`, `@JsonTypeInfo(use = Id.CLASS)` | `ObjectMapper` config, DTOs | Payload selects the type | DES-02 |
| Sensitive fields in `Serializable` classes without `transient` | DTOs, entities | Data leakage via serialization | DES-07 |
| JSP `<%= request.getParameter(…) %>`, `out.print(param)`, JSTL `<c:out escapeXml="false">`; XML built by concatenation | JSP, servlets | Unencoded output | JVA-07, XSS-01 |
| Thymeleaf `th:utext` with user data | templates | Escape hatch (Thymeleaf not localized; note gap for defaults) | XSS-02 |
| Global "XSS filter" servlet/filter that encodes request parameters | `web.xml`, filters | Interceptor instead of output encoding | XSS-10 |
| `new File(base, input)` / `Paths.get(input)` without normalization and prefix check | file services | Path traversal | JVA-08 |
| `MultipartFile.getOriginalFilename()` in a storage path; type decided by `getContentType()` only | upload controllers | Client filename/type trusted | FU-04, FU-03 |
| `ZipInputStream` loops without byte/entry limits | upload/import code | Zip bomb | JVA-11, FU-05 |
| Spring Boot `spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size=-1` / `max-request-size=-1` | `application*.properties/yml` | Unlimited upload size (explicit only) | FU-05 |
| Uploads written under `src/main/webapp`, `static/` or `public/` | upload code | Uploads in webroot | FU-07 |
| `Double.parseDouble(input)` in monetary or limit logic without `isNaN`/`isInfinite` checks | services | NaN/Infinity accepted | JVA-09 |
| Request DTOs without Bean Validation constraints (`@Size`, `@Min`, `@Max`, `@Pattern`) or without `@Valid` | DTOs, controllers | Missing field rules | IV-02, IV-07 |
| `Pattern.compile` with nested quantifiers on unbounded input; `find()` used for full validation | validators | ReDoS / partial match | IV-08 |

## File: `references/standards/java-input.md`

*Load rule: JVA-01…15. Load when language `java` is detected.*

### Java / JDK / Spring Data JPA input & injection guidance — localized summary

- Applies when language `java` is detected. Spring Data JPA elements (JVA-14, JVA-15) apply when `spring-data-jpa` or
  `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa` is a dependency; JDK, Oracle-guideline and OWASP elements always.
- Level: a vendor element takes the level of the OWASP element it supports, or `SHOULD` when the vendor only
  recommends. **(Default)** marks an element that states API behaviour or a default; cite the OWASP element it supports
  and name the JVA element in the recommendation. Where vendor guidance is weaker than an OWASP element, the OWASP
  element decides. Severity rules are in `../../SKILL.md`.
- Defaults stated here are the only Java defaults a worker may rely on. Spring Boot multipart limits, Thymeleaf,
  Hibernate native APIs and SnakeYAML version defaults are **not** localized: report only explicit insecure settings
  there, and add a `localized-standard-gap` note for a missing setting.

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| JVA-01 | MUST | JPA/Hibernate isn't blanket protection: JPQL/HQL must be parameterized too. | `em.createQuery("… " + v)` | SEC-II-02 |
| JVA-02 | MUST | Don't deserialize untrusted data — including data read back from a database. | `readObject` on DB blobs or request streams | SEC-II-09 |
| JVA-03 | MUST | INJECT-2: avoid dynamic SQL; use `PreparedStatement`/`CallableStatement`, not `Statement`, or a well-written higher-level library. | `Statement.executeQuery(sql + v)` | SEC-II-02 |
| JVA-04 | MUST | INJECT-4: no untrusted data on the command line of new processes (option injection via leading `-`/`/`, argument splitting). | `Runtime.exec`/`ProcessBuilder` with request data | SEC-II-04 |
| JVA-05 | MUST | INJECT-5/DOS-1: restrict XML inclusion (DTD system entities, XInclude, XSLT `document()`) and set `XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING` with reasonable limits. | XInclude enabled; FSP explicitly `false` | SEC-II-05 |
| JVA-06 | MUST | INJECT-8: don't run untrusted code: `javax.script` evaluation, XSLT extension functions (FSP disables them), JNDI lookups with untrusted names (LDAP/RMI remote class loading). | `ScriptEngine.eval(input)`; `new InitialContext().lookup(input)` | SEC-II-04 |
| JVA-07 | MUST | INJECT-3: sanitize/encode untrusted data in generated HTML/XML with a library, taking particular care in JSP. | `out.print(request.getParameter(…))` in JSP/servlets; XML built by string concatenation | SEC-II-08 |
| JVA-08 | MUST | INPUT-1: validate untrusted input before use, including `../` directory traversal in file names; validate again immediately before a security-sensitive use. | `new File(base, request.getParameter("name"))` | SEC-II-01 |
| JVA-09 | SHOULD | INJECT-9: reject NaN/Infinity from untrusted floating-point input before sensitive calculations. | `Double.valueOf(input)` feeding prices/limits unchecked | SEC-II-01 |
| JVA-10 | MUST | SERIAL-6: filter untrusted serial data with serialization filters (allowlist per context; `ObjectInputFilter`, `jdk.serialFilter`). | `ObjectInputStream` with no filter on any external stream | SEC-II-09 |
| JVA-11 | SHOULD | DOS-1: limit decompressed size rather than trusting compressed size or metadata (zip bombs). | `ZipInputStream` loops with no byte/entry limit | SEC-II-06 |
| JVA-12 | MUST | (Default) FSP is on by default, but the JDK doesn't restrict external connections unless FSP is set **explicitly** through the API or External Access Properties are set; a factory parsing untrusted XML with neither (nor `disallow-doctype-decl`) fails XML-02. | `DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance()` / `SAXParserFactory` / `XMLInputFactory` / `TransformerFactory` on untrusted input with no explicit settings | SEC-II-05 |
| JVA-13 | SHOULD | Disable DTDs (`jdk.xml.dtd.support` or `disallow-doctype-decl`) when not needed, tighten processing limits, and resolve required external resources only through a resolver/catalog. | DTD support left on for parsers that never need it | SEC-II-05 |
| JVA-14 | MUST | (Default) Spring Data JPA rejects `Sort` orders containing functions by default; `JpaSort.unsafe(…)` bypasses that check and must never carry user-supplied sort input. | `JpaSort.unsafe(request.getParameter("sort"))` | SEC-II-03 |
| JVA-15 | SHOULD | (Default) Derived `LIKE` queries (`Containing`, `StartingWith`, …) escape wildcard characters in arguments; hand-written `@Query` `LIKE` with concatenation doesn't. | `@Query("… LIKE '%" + …)`; native queries with concatenation | SEC-II-03 |
